text:
sasha: Heads-up — trying to onboard folded-llama-13b from HF. Conversion failed: tokenizer lost special chat tokens and model requires trust_remote_code. Also seeing weird token padding when running chat templates. Anyone seen this combo before?

alex: do you have the original config.json and tokenizer files? auto_map can drop custom classes if trust_remote_code isn't allowed.

maria: paste of the short error from redwood-import run:
```
ERROR: TokenizerError: unknown special token '<|assistant|>' when building chat template
Conversion aborted: model requires trust_remote_code=True to instantiate custom modules
```

infra-bot: redwood-import job #4821 failed (exit 1). Logs: s3://redwood-import/logs/4821.txt

alex: two quick checks — 1) open the HF model dir and look for `tokenizer.json` or `special_tokens_map.json`; 2) if model has custom AutoModel classes, run conversion with `--trust-remote-code` so auto_map can instantiate them. Example: 
```
redwood-import --src hf://folded-llama-13b --dst redwood://folded-llama-13b --trust-remote-code
```

jong: fyi chat templates expect consistent special tokens like `<|user|>` / `<|assistant|>` or the `role` mapping in the template. If tokenizer lost `additional_special_tokens` the renderer will pad tokens incorrectly. Quick hack that worked for me: load tokenizer locally and re-add tokens then save: 
```
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('...')
tok.add_special_tokens({'additional_special_tokens': ['<|user|>', '<|assistant|>']})
tok.save_pretrained('./fixed-tokenizer')
```

sasha: tried that — re-adding tokens fixed template padding, chat formatting now looks correct, but quantized int4 build has serious quality regression: replies are hallucinating short facts and attention seems truncated.

maria: what quant backend? bitsandbytes + qlora or native Redwood int4 conversion?

sasha: followed the Redwood optimize suggestion: `--quantize int4 --backend bnb` during import. The loss jumps on eval sets vs fp16 baseline.

alex: two things — 1) some custom model classes implement attention/rotary differently; trust_remote_code may instantiate a PyTorch class that the quantizer doesn't fully support. 2) try exporting with `--no-opt` to keep fp16 kernels for sensitive layers and quantize the rest. Example: 
```
redwood-import --src hf://folded-llama-13b --quantize int4 --bnb-keep-fp16-layers 'q_proj,k_proj' --trust-remote-code
```

devex-bot: docs: https://redwood.ai/docs/import#trust-remote-code and run `redwood inspect-model folded-llama-13b` to preview tokenizer + config before committing.

maria: quick repro note: when I tried `--trust-remote-code` without `--bnb-keep-fp16-layers` the eval BLEU/ROUGE numbers dropped ~12% vs baseline on our intent classification set. With the keep-fp16 tweak it's back within 2-3%.

jong: if the HF model overrides `modeling_utils` or attention math, auto_map can create a class where some ops are in Python-level wrappers — those don't quantize well. If possible ask model author for a lightweight export or try the HF `--safe-serialize` flag to produce standard layers.

sasha: good notes — plan: 1) patch tokenizer and re-save to preserve special tokens, 2) re-import with `--trust-remote-code` + selective fp16 keep list, 3) run canary with rollback policy. Will report metrics.

alex: for the canary rollout you can use runtime routing: 
```
rollout:
  - percent: 5
    model: folded-llama-13b-int4
    fallback: folded-llama-13b-fp16
    metrics: [latency, perplexity]
```

sasha: thanks — will try that tomorrow and share eval graphs. :thumbsup:
